sections.title: Home
sections.question: What should the first screen say when you come back? Everyone agrees it opens on what is new. The difference is how loud the lead is.
take: All four directions moved away from today's grid of tests to "what's new first". They differ in volume: A a quiet list, B coloured step cards, C one quote as a headline, D one playable moment.
My read: A's quiet list, with D's "worth watching" moment as its first item when there is one. C's quote works as that moment's headline.

tiles.label: A · Studio
tiles.idea: What's new as a list with real thumbnails and one dot per session; the first run puts the three inputs right on the page.
works: Calm, and the real thumbnails replace icon tiles
Session dots: status for six sessions in one glance
First run is the input itself (paste, drop, connect), not three cards
doesnt: Three columns compete (what's new, tests, sites)
The coloured squares beside each test in the sidebar are colour-coding again
Plan usage block at the bottom is noise on every page

tiles.label: B · Colour
tiles.idea: What's new split by step (Publish, Test, Review), each in its colour; a loop meter shows where each test has got to.
works: You know what kind of news it is before you read it
The loop meter is a nice, honest progress mark
No colour in the nav, as asked
doesnt: Three coloured cards in a row is close to the AI pattern
Tests and sites tables repeat each other
A lot of colour for a page you see daily

tiles.label: C · Story
tiles.idea: A front page: the newest thing a tester said is the headline, tests and sites as an index on the right. No sidebar.
works: The most human home: her words first
Top bar instead of sidebar gives the reading column room
Highlighter and tally marks instead of pills
doesnt: One lead story hides the rest when several tests run
Roman numerals and italics are decoration (the team agrees)
Without a sidebar the list of tests is one click further away

tiles.label: D · Replay
tiles.idea: Opens on one moment worth watching, cued to 03:08; tests drawn as reels; the loop line runs along the bottom.
works: Shows the product's value every visit
Reels: each bar is a session, to scale
The bottom line is the same thing as the homepage scrubber and the video
doesnt: Dark everywhere is heavy for daily admin work
Small, dense type
A playing clip can distract when you only came to copy a link

tiles.label: E · App UI round
img: Layouts A, B, C plus states
tiles.idea: The previous round: three home layouts and every state (first run, loading, drafts, phone).
works: Covers every state, which the directions don't
Draft rule: only real input becomes a draft
doesnt: Looks like a generic template next to A to D
Icons in pastel boxes in the feed (the pattern you flagged)

tiles.label: Today's app
doesnt: Grid of empty drafts with made-up names
Numbers that say 0% before anything happened

sections.title: Sessions
sections.question: How do you see and move between the sessions of one test?
take: A, B and C agree: a numbered list with each tester's first words, numbers that never change, and J / K to move. D adds something none of the others have: every session on one shared clock, so the 03:08 cluster across four testers shows before you press play.
My read: C's list (their words, big numbers) with B's friction ticks per row, and D's shared clock as a "Compare" view on top.

tiles.label: A · Studio
tiles.idea: A calm table with a peek panel on the right; status is a word with its own mark.
works: Peek panel: read the summary without leaving the list
"First friction, in their words" column
doesnt: The length strip on top adds little (the team would drop it)
Very close to today's structure; little new

tiles.label: B · Colour
tiles.idea: Length drawn to scale with a tick per friction point; the test header turns mint on Review tabs.
works: Friction ticks per row are the clearest small signal
Selected row in the same blue as the dot
doesnt: Header changing colour per tab feels jumpy (the team agrees)

tiles.label: C · Story
tiles.idea: A contents page: each session listed by its first line in the tester's words.
works: Most readable; you can choose what to watch from the words alone
"Next session" teaser at the end of each one
doesnt: No sense of where in the session things went wrong
Feels like a document if there are 40 sessions

tiles.label: D · Replay
tiles.idea: All sessions as tracks on one clock, like an editor; selected one previews on top.
works: Unique: shows patterns across testers before watching
Each status looks different (waveform, hatching, flat line)
doesnt: Squashes when lengths vary a lot
Dark, editor-like; may feel technical

tiles.label: Today's app
img: Live: says no sessions while two exist
doesnt: Sessions tab can say "no sessions" while they exist (bug B2)

sections.title: Session review
sections.question: Watch first or read first? This is the most important screen and the real choice of the round.
take: A, B and D put the recording first; C puts her words first and docks the recording. You liked C's calm analysis view and D's timeline line, which pull in different directions.

My read: C's article layout as the default (headline from her words, summary, transcript with friction points in the margin), with D's timeline as the player bar of the docked recording, and one switch to make the recording big.
Note for C: the yellow rule down the left of the summary and the margin notes is a mild version of the side-stripe pattern; I would remove it.

tiles.label: A · Studio
tiles.idea: Recording left on the Review wash, transcript right following the playback, summary and priorities under.
works: True to the app: word highlight only on playback, no cursor
Friction cards jump to their moment
doesnt: Three areas compete for attention
Transcript is small and secondary

tiles.label: B · Colour
tiles.idea: Recording first; friction points are mint ticks on the timeline and mint times in the list.
works: Ticks on the timeline match the list
Clear task markers
doesnt: Almost the same layout as A
The blue word highlight is harsh at reading size

tiles.label: C · Story
tiles.idea: The session reads like an article: her words as the headline, summary as the standfirst, transcript as the body, friction in the margin.
works: The calmest way to understand a session
Friction point sits beside the line that caused it
Headline is her own words
doesnt: Yellow left rules (side-stripe pattern)
Recording is small; watching is secondary

tiles.label: D · Replay
tiles.idea: The recording is the page; tasks and friction points on its timeline; light variant included.
works: Watching is the core value, and this shows it
Timeline with tasks and markers is the best player bar of the four
doesnt: Transcript squeezed into a column
Lots going on under the player

tiles.label: Today's app
doesnt: Recording on a separate page from the findings

sections.title: Publish from a prompt
sections.question: The connector flow: connect once, copy the prompt, wait for the chat, published. Which look and how much detail?
take: All four land on the same flow, so this is a choice of look and detail, not of flow. All keep Claude in its own panel outside Aero.
Detail ranges from C (calm, four lines) to D (a live log with clock times). D is the most reassuring while waiting, but its file sizes are too technical for most people.

tiles.label: A · Studio
tiles.idea: One page that keeps its history; each step ticks off in place; ends on "Now test it".
works: Ends on the next step, not a dashboard
Short "What the prompt does" notes
doesnt: Shows the steps twice (cards and page)

tiles.label: B · Colour
tiles.idea: Publish is sunflower; four numbered steps; tabs switch between Figma, HTML and prompt.
works: Clearest numbering
"Share the test" when the prompt already made one
doesnt: The yellow is strong for a whole page

tiles.label: C · Story
tiles.idea: A short numbered log; the published site set like a title page.
works: Calmest
Real thumbnail of the published page
doesnt: Roman numerals

tiles.label: D · Replay
tiles.idea: While waiting, a log with clock times fills the empty player.
works: Most reassuring while you wait
Empty player fills with your prototype when live
doesnt: "Receiving files, 412 KB" is too technical
Dark

tiles.label: Today's app
doesnt: Lands on setup fields, not on the link to share

sections.title: Upload HTML or zip
sections.question: Drop, uploading, published with address and version, then "Now test it".
take: Again the same flow everywhere. Worth keeping from all: the version list with roll back, and "Now test it" as the one next step.
The upload limits the teams wrote (50 MB, 100 MB) are placeholders. The code has a 4.5 MB request cap on one path; the real limit needs checking before any copy uses a number.

tiles.label: A · Studio
works: Version table with roll back on each row
Calm file list while uploading
doesnt: Limit placeholder

tiles.label: B · Colour
works: Settings (password, domain, badge) beside versions
doesnt: Sunflower drop zone close to a pastel box

tiles.label: C · Story
works: Published page reads like a title page
doesnt: Drawn preview of the site is simplified

tiles.label: D · Replay
works: The bottom line doubles as the upload progress bar
The live site shown as testers will see it
doesnt: Dark frame around a light site

tiles.label: Today's app
doesnt: Free sites say "Live" after they have gone offline (B13)

sections.title: Review across sessions
sections.question: What to fix first, across six sessions.
take: My read: C's plain-English headline ("People found sending easy. Almost nobody found their cards."), then a numbered "what to fix first" with counts shown as A's session dots or B's squares and playable quotes. D's "where people got stuck" chart as an optional view.
D's ordering by "how long it held them" and "where testers disagreed" need data we do not save today; treat them as proposals.

tiles.label: A · Studio
works: Session dots show who said what, so "4 of 5" is visible
doesnt: Summary wash box at the top is soft but vague

tiles.label: B · Colour
works: Count squares are clear
What worked and where testers disagreed, side by side
doesnt: Mint header again

tiles.label: C · Story
works: The headline sentence is the best summary of a test in any version
doesnt: Little visual proof; it is all words

tiles.label: D · Replay
works: Overlay on one clock is strong visual proof
Quotes as playable clips
doesnt: Needs data not saved today

tiles.label: Today's app
doesnt: Insights stuck or crashing (B3 to B5)

sections.title: The flow: from prompt to first session
sections.question: Four different flows. This is an information architecture choice, not a visual one.
take: A and C arrived separately at the same idea: one page per prototype that fills in as you go (published, test link, sessions, review). Today Sites and Tests are separate places.

My read: decide this first. If yes, "Pocket" is one object with Publish, Test and Review tabs, and Sites and Tests stop being separate lists. B's stepper and D's timeline are then ways of showing progress on that page.

tiles.label: A · Studio: one page that fills in
works: Nothing to navigate; each step lands as a row
doesnt: Merges Sites and Tests: a real IA change

tiles.label: B · Colour: a colour stepper
works: The canvas colour tells you which step you are in
doesnt: More screens; feels like a wizard

tiles.label: C · Story: a page that keeps a log
works: Times on every step; history stays readable
doesnt: Log can get long

tiles.label: D · Replay: player-first, one line
works: The whole journey is one timeline; best for the video
doesnt: As app navigation it is abstract

sections.title: Marketing versions of components
sections.question: The step that was missing: five real components (session card, friction quote, site card, test link, transcript line) at 1.5 to 2x, with less detail, then a hero and a social card built only from them.
take: B's rule is the one to keep whatever the look: a component never picks its own colour; it takes the colour of the step it sits on. That is what lets one session card work in the app, on the site and in a video.
The friction quote with the word highlight is the strongest marketing piece in all four; it is also "In their own words".

tiles.label: A · Studio
works: Washes carry from app to site unchanged
"In their own words" social card
doesnt: Hero stack is a little busy

tiles.label: B · Colour
works: Step colour explains before you read
Three-column social card
doesnt: Close to three pastel cards

tiles.label: C · Story
works: The highlighted quote is the hero
Most restrained
doesnt: Little colour; may look plain on social

tiles.label: D · Replay
works: Dark tiles stand out on a light page
Player and waveform are ready for video
doesnt: Dark everything in marketing

sections.title: Buttons
sections.question: Not decided. Eight families, each in five real moments: create footer, session header, tester screen, task panel, hero, dark surface.
take: Findings: glass falls apart when a button sits across two backgrounds; clear glass gets thin over yellow and orange; disabled glass looks broken. Glass is at its best where controls float over a prototype.

My read: ink solid as the main button, ink-tinted glass only where controls float over a prototype (tester task panel, player). Blue stays the dot, the playhead and links. The live page shows the glass properly (screenshots flatten it).

tiles.label: Button families
tiles.idea: Ink solid, Aero blue, ink outline, quiet text, soft tint, glass clear, glass ink, glass blue.

sections.title: Logo in use
sections.question: Not decided. Seven options, at size, 24px, favicon 32 and 16, then in the sidebar, tester footer, share email, browser tab and site nav.
take: In a browser tab every option becomes the same tile, so the favicon matters more than the wordmark; "A." is the strongest at 16px.
"Made with Aero." puts a full stop mid-sentence. If "Aero." wins, the tester footer may need the wordmark without the dot, or the dot mark.

intro: You said a step was missing: seeing each main screen in every direction and deciding what works before tightening components. This is that step.

Each row is one screen. A, B, C and D are the four round 5 directions, each redrawn across the whole app by its own team (new screens, with the round 5 version underneath where there was one). E is the app UI round. Today is the live app. Then the flow, the marketing kit, buttons and the logo.

Click any picture for full size. Mark each tile Keep, Parts of it or Drop, with a note if it helps; I read your marks before the next round. The live pages (with real glass and hover) are linked at the bottom.
roles: home, sessions and the one-page-per-prototype question
layout, type, status without pills or icon boxes
every label against the tone of voice
the marketing kit and composed hero and card
patterns: White cards with a coloured stripe down one side
Rows of three identical icon cards
Pills on everything; stock photos of people
recommend: Use A (Studio) as the app's look: light, calm, colour only in soft washes. It held up on every screen.
Take C's session as an article (her words as the headline, friction in the margin) and C's plain-English review headline.
Take D's timeline line (player bar, loop line, flow line) and the "worth watching" moment on Home; offer D's shared clock as a Compare view.
Take B's rule: components take the colour of the step they sit on. Use count squares or session dots for "4 of 5".
Decide the IA question first: one page per prototype, with Publish, Test and Review on it, instead of separate Sites and Tests.
Buttons: ink solid; glass only where controls float over a prototype. Logo: keep "Aero." with an "A." favicon, and check the tester footer wording.
Then tighten the app UI round into these components and their marketing versions, and add them to the /aero showcase.
